anchor.address: Font de la Plaça d'Espanya, Barcelona

reference.streetview_capture: Not checked in Street View yet; looked at openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photos from 2019 to July 2025 (docs/places/espanya.md lists them)
notes: MAP DATA: OpenStreetMap (osm.json, fetched 2026-10-30 through the OSM API bbox call: Overpass was busy). The anchor is the centre of Jujol's fountain.

Turned 162°: Avinguda de la Reina Maria Cristina (bearing 153°) runs straight up the screen between the two Venetian towers, towards Montjuïc and the Palau Nacional; Las Arenas is at the bottom, nearest the camera; Gran Via crosses the screen from left to right.

Square: a roundabout about 120 m across between kerbs (the island's edge about 41 m from the centre, the ring road four to six lanes wide); 34,000 m² in all. Five roads meet: Gran Via (both ways), Paral·lel, Creu Coberta, Tarragona and Maria Cristina.

Island: an oval lawn ringed by red-leaved shrubs, the fountain on a triangular basin. Since late 2024 the island is a works site for the FGC L8 extension (OSM landuse=construction 'Perllongament FGC Llobregat-Anoia'): yellow plastic barriers round the whole island, dug soil and blue tarps, the fountain dry; the roundabout down to four lanes in places. The tunnel-boring shaft and its acoustic shed are on Gran Via between Llançà and Vilamarí, behind Las Arenas (2026).

Fountain (Font dels Tres Mars, Josep Maria Jujol, 1929): grey and cream stone, three basins on a triangle, a central edicle with three niches (Ebre, Guadalquivir and Tajo by Miquel Blay), three Corinthian columns, bronze groups at the corners (the Oslé brothers), a bronze brazier with three Victories on top (Frederic Llobet), iron lanterns. About 30 m across the basins; the top about 20 m high (estimate).

Venetian towers (Ramon Reventós, 1927-29): two identical towers 47 m high on a 7.2 m square base, about 33 m apart centre to centre, one each side of the avenue. A slightly battered cream base with a door, a shaft of exposed red brick with three recessed arched channels per face and slit windows, a wide cream cornice on brackets, a loggia of Corinthian columns, a pyramidal copper roof gone dark grey-green.

Las Arenas (August Font i Carreras, 1900; Richard Rogers and Alonso-Balaguer, shopping centre opened 2011): a neo-Mudéjar bullring 100 m across in red-orange brick, two tiers of horseshoe arches with cream and brick voussoirs, bands of coloured ceramic triangles, saw-tooth brick cornices and crenellations, the main gate tower with ARENAS DE BARCELONA and the city's arms. The old facade stands on a grey concrete band carried by red steel V struts over a glazed ground floor with purple panels; above it a flat dish roof with a red steel rim and a round public terrace walk; a red panoramic lift tower outside, facing the square.

Fira (1929 Exhibition palaces): the Palau de Comunicacions i Transports (east) and the Palau del Vestit (west) face the square with curved fronts of giant columns in warm pinkish limestone, glass between them, a balustrade with urns, obelisk pinnacles and big arched doors; grey sheet roofs behind. In front, a wide forecourt in salmon concrete slabs and grey granite steps; cypresses beside the towers.

Around: Hotel Catalonia Barcelona Plaza (grey stone grid of square windows, 9 storeys) between Creu Coberta and Tarragona; the Mossos d'Esquadra station (light grey offices) between Gran Via and Paral·lel; Eixample and Sants blocks of six to ten storeys; Torre Allianz behind on Tarragona.

Street: wide asphalt with many lanes, arrows and BUS markings; grey granite slabs and panot on the sidewalks; tall lamp masts with three or four heads; traffic lights on curved poles; plane trees on Gran Via and Tarragona; benches and Bicing docks.
Traffic: yellow-and-black taxis queuing on Tarragona, TMB red buses, turquoise interurban buses, the red tourist bus, coaches for the fairs.

Background: up the avenue, its median fountains, the Magic Fountain (about 480 m), Puig i Cadafalch's four columns, the stairs and cascades, the Palau Nacional (MNAC, about 820 m) with its dome and towers, Montjuïc's pines and Calatrava's white communications tower. Out of reach: drawn as a backdrop.

places.label: Mirar las torres
lines: Las torres venecianas. Cuarenta y siete metros de ladrillo, copiadas del campanario de San Marcos.
Las levantaron para la Exposición del 29 y tenían que derribarlas después. Siguen aquí.

places.label: Mirar la avenida
lines: La avenida sube recta hasta el Palau Nacional, allá arriba en Montjuïc.
En medio, la Font Màgica. Hoy está callada.

places.label: Mirar la fuente
lines: La fuente de los tres mares, de Jujol. Seca, y rodeada de vallas amarillas.
Las obras de la L8. Llevan tanto tiempo que ya son parte de la plaza.

places.label: Mirar Las Arenas
lines: Las Arenas. Una plaza de toros hecha centro comercial, levantada sobre patas rojas.
Arriba hay un mirador redondo. Desde ahí se ve toda la plaza.

places.label: Mirar la Fira
lines: El Palau de Comunicacions. Columnas como troncos y nadie entre ellas.
Hoy no hay feria. Solo palomas en la escalinata.
